Pishchana Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Pishchana, Ukraine

Not demolished. Existing since at least 1864 per gravestone dating, this cemetery appears on Russian maps from 1912-13 and 1927; a postwar memorial marks a mass grave on the grounds, and today's territory covers only about half its prewar extent. Jewish settlement began in the early 19th century; population reached 750 (25%) by 1887 and 870 by 1897, with a synagogue operating from 1889 and Jews active in crafts and trade. By 1914, Jewish-owned businesses included a pharmacy, bakery, two timber stores, two mills, and nearly 50 shops; population rose slightly to 902 by 1923, settling at 466 (8%) by 1939. German-Romanian occupation in summer 1941 established a ghetto holding almost 500 Jews, eventually transferred to the Bershad ghetto.
